screenings.title: Lost Highway
screenings.description: Few filmmakers have shown themselves so adept at plumbing the depths of the subconscious without coming up for air as Lynch, whose Lost Highway—inspired loosely by still-fresh coverage of the O. J. Simpson trial—begins as a dark domestic drama concerning a sexually incompetent saxophonist (Bill Pullman) and his wife (Patricia Arquette), morphs into a movie about a cocksman mechanic (Balthazar Getty) who gets involved with a gangster’s girl (Arquette, again), and ends with an unleashing of apocalyptic, purgative flame… Whether you take it as a cinematic depiction of a psychogenic fugue state or a free-associative disgorging of images from Hollywood’s id, Lynch’s film has the pull of a whirlpool and the terrible logic of a nightmare.

screenings.title: The Brood
screenings.description: In The Brood, the bitter divorce between the mentally disturbed Nola (Samantha Eggar) and her ex-husband Frank (Art Hindle) was pretty messy, so it should be a good sign that she’s finally getting professional help from the renowned Dr. Hal Raglan (Oliver Reed)—but Frank can’t help but notice that people on Nola’s long list of enemies keep dying at the hands of asexual, dwarfish assassins, and so he starts to wonder what exactly the experimental therapy practiced at Dr. Raglan’s Somafree Institute consists of… Written while Cronenberg was in the midst of his own divorce and custody battle, The Brood is a brutal, bracing airing of anxieties gussied up in grindhouse trappings.

screenings.title: The Reflecting Skin
screenings.description: Growing up in the 1950s in small-town Idaho, 8-year-old Seth and his friends play a prank on the town recluse, a mysterious English widow named Dolphin Blue (Tony winner Lindsay Duncan). After his father tells him stories of vampires, Seth becomes convinced Dolphin is a vampire, stealing the souls of his neighborhood friends one by one. When his older brother Cameron (Oscar nominee Viggo Mortensen in one of his first starring roles), returns home from military service in the Pacific and takes a liking to Dolphin, Seth feels it’s up to him to save Cameron from his friends’ fate. With stunning visuals recalling Edward Hopper paintings and its surreal blend of horror and humor, THE REFLECTING SKIN is a “stunningly beautiful…Gothic masterpiece” (The Guardian)!”

screenings.title: The Holy Mountain
screenings.description: The follow-up to his Midnight Movie sensation El Topo, writer-director Alejandro Jodorowsky’s THE HOLY MOUNTAIN caused a scandal at the 1973 Cannes Film Festival with its flood of sacrilegious imagery, existential symbolism and outrageous violence. Once again, Jodorowsky plays the allegorically named lead, “The Alchemist,” who assembles a group of people from all walks of life and renames them for the planets in the solar system. Putting his recruits through strange mystical rites and divesting them of their worldly baggage, he leads them on a trip to Lotus Island to ascend the Holy Mountain and displace the immortal gods who secretly rule the universe. This gorgeous new digital restoration, overseen by the filmmaker himself, returns Jodorowsky’s most visually extravagant film to all its trippy splendor.

screenings.description: “Poetic, political, and above all incontrovertibly material” [The New Yorker], Kogonada’s fourth feature, the experimental drama zi, follows the title character, played by Michelle Mao, a concert violinist whose aimless peregrinations through the streets of Hong Kong are interrupted by visions of what may be either her past or future, a condition she attempts to explain to a new American acquaintance (Haley Lu Richardson, Columbus) while a stranger (Jin Ha) observes the pair from a distance. A valentine to the textures and colors of the Fragrant Harbor as seen by night, featuring music by the late Ryuichi Sakamoto, the formally audacious, shot-on-the-fly zi is a film of unusual delicacy and reserve, one whose air of mystery abides long after the credits have rolled.

screenings.title: Benedetta
screenings.description: Inspired by the life of Benedetta Carlini, a nun of 17th-century Tuscany whose claims of mystic visions drew the attention of church higher-ups, their investigations eventually revealing a verboten sexual relationship between Carlini and one of her fellow nuns and leading to her imprisonment, Verhoeven’s earthy, irreverent film immerses one in the squelchy squalor and earthly delights of Counter-Reformation era Europe, with Virginie Efira a revelation in the title role and Charlotte Rampling, as the abbess of the convent, conveying roiling inner turmoil beneath a cooly composed exterior. An examination of the difficult relationship between religious submission and sexual liberation, featuring some of the most memorable foley sounds in recent cinema.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: The Souvenir
screenings.description: Hogg, who has quietly established herself as one of the finest UK filmmakers working, offers a keenly observed, sometimes bruising portrayal of toxic romance set in ’80s Britain, starring Honor Swinton Byrne (daughter of Tilda, who plays the character’s patrician mother) as Julie, an aspiring filmmaker who begins a relationship with Anthony (Tom Burke), a slightly older man in the employ of the Foreign Office whose attractive intelligence and worldliness can’t compensate for the fact that he is an addict and a natural manipulator. Hogg’s usual compositional rigor works in service of enormously empathic semi-autobiographical storytelling, using flashback inserts in order to plumb the psychology of a hopelessly dysfunctional relationship.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Victor decides to rent a country house away from the city, but the couple’s summer idyll becomes complicated by his involvement with a younger model. One of the very first fictional features by an African-American woman, Losing Ground remains a stunning and powerful work of art for being a funny, brilliant, and personal member of indie cinema canon.

screenings.title: Maîtres Anciens – Comédie
screenings.description: “Like Reger – the character [Austrian novelist and playwright] Thomas Bernhard placed on a museum bench facing a painting by Tintoretto, an ‘Old Master’ if ever there was one – an actor finds himself alone and thwarted after a notorious virus forces the indefinite closure of theaters. He wanders through an empty auditorium, paces the now-useless backstage areas, and bursts out into a street haunted by masked passersby. Having persuaded a firefighter to keep watch over him and his explosives, he pours out – to the guard and the surrounding silence alike – his loathing for, among other things, Heideggerians, a lack of punctuality, people who admire rather than respect, and the State’s appropriation of children. At the intersection of cinema and theater, despair and the will to survive, 1980s Austria and 2020s France, Bernhard’s text takes on a new resonance: ‘And as for culture in this country, your stomach exists only to turn.’” –Marie Hermann, FIDMarseillePreceded by:Mathieu Amalric C’EST PRESQUE AU BOUT DU MONDE (2015, 16 min, digital. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: The Cobweb
screenings.description: Dir. Vincente Minnelli. 1955, 134 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Lauren Bacall, Richard Widmark, Gloria Grahame, Lillian Gish, Charles Boyer, John Kerr, Susan Strasberg, Oscar Levant. An essential Minnelli, featuring maybe his most wildly stacked cast, The Cobweb confidently offers up a nearly undefinable mix of the restrained and the truly eccentric. Set in a psychiatric hospital, where the staff is likely more unsettled than the patients, this Cinemascope, Eastmancolor contraption details the fallout after the head doctor’s wife does the unthinkable: she changes the color of the library’s drapes! Long read as a perfect auteur text for Minnelli (who got his start as a window dresser), The Cobweb is a gorgeously shot, low-boil soap opera that’s a must for any 1950s melodrama completist. screenings.title: Far From Afghanistan
screenings.description: Boston-based filmmaker and former Harvard Film Archive curator John Gianvito had made a few films before the 20th century became the 21st, but he would wind up emerging as one of the definitive filmmakers of the current century during its first decade. His six years of work on Gulf War I cri de cœur The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein wound up serving as one of the definitive commentaries on the upcoming century when it premiered in 2001. Mad Songs served as a work of inadvertent commentary on the bloodlust spurred by the Twin Tower attacks, and the Gulf War II that was going to come about as a result. It was also a work of intensely personal cinephilia-inspired curation: Griffith- and Wyler-adjacent structuring of multiple war-at-home storylines was melded with archival footage and performance documentary, resulting in a bold and sprawling hybrid work. Despite fierce advocacy from notable champions in Chantal Akerman, Peter Watkins, Jonathan Rosenbaum, and Dennis Lim, it was not an easy film to see in 2001 and it has not gotten much easier since. He’d take another six years to make his next film, this time decidedly aimed at the domestic. Profit Motive and the Whispering Wind (2007) was a film whose more minimalist scale and running time didn’t reduce its power. Its simultaneously rousing and despairing analysis, courtesy of Howard Zinn, marked a turn towards a more domestic issue: how America eats its rabble rousers but leaves a tribute to them later. The groundwork laid by the champions of Mad Songs resulted in Profit Motive finding more of an audience, and it subsequently being named the Best Experimental Film of 2007 by the National Society of Film Critics.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: 5 Short Films Supported by the Displacement Film Fund
screenings.description: Actor and producer Cate Blanchett, together with International Film Festival Rotterdam’s (IFFR) Hubert Bals Fund, will host the New York premiere of the Displacement Film Fund’s inaugural slate of films on November 11 at Film Forum. Co-founded and led by Blanchett, the Displacement Film Fund (DFF) was established to champion and fund the work of displaced filmmakers, or filmmakers with a proven track record in creating authentic stories focused on the experiences of displaced people. Timely, surprising and intimate, the shorts in this critically acclaimed collection are directed by internationally renowned filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine), Mo Harawe (Somalia-Austria), Hasan Kattan (Syria), Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran), and Shahrbanoo Sadat (Afghanistan). All five films will be presented at Film Forum, with filmmakers Maryna Er Gorbach and Mo Harawe in person at each program. After premiering at the 2026 International Film Festival Rotterdam, this collection was invited to the London, Sao Paulo (Mostra), and Tokyo international film festivals. The films will be released on The New Yorker this November. Rotation dir. Maryna Er Gorbach (Ukraine, Turkey) 12 min. Rotation is a therapeutic hypnosis ritual experienced by a young Ukrainian woman who shifted from civilian life to military service. She needs support to adapt to the displaced reality she now lives in. Gorbach’s KLONDIKE was Winner of the World Cinema Dramatic Directing Award at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival. Super Afghan Gym dir. Shahrbanoo Sadat (Germany) 14 min. In a gym in downtown Kabul, a group of housewives gather during the only hour of the day reserved for women. They train at lunchtime behind closed doors, talking about body norms and their daily life. Sadat’s most recent film, NO GOOD MEN, was the opening night selection of the 2026 Berlin Film Festival. Allies in Exile dir. Hasan Kattan (United Kingdom) 40 min. For 14 years, Syrian filmmakers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi have journeyed together through war and storytelling. Confined inside a UK asylum hotel, Hasan and Fadi document a new chapter shaped not by bombs, but by waiting, bureaucracy, and exile. Amid rising anti-refugee hostility, they turn the camera inward exploring friendship and displacement and how filming itself becomes an act of survival when the future is so uncertain. Kattan served as cinematographer on the Oscar®-winning The White Helmets and assistant director on the Oscar®-nominated LAST MEN IN ALEPPO. Whispers of a Burning Scent dir. Mo Harawe (Somalia, Austria, Germany) 27 min. On the day of a decisive court hearing and an important wedding performance, a quiet wedding musician finds his private life exposed to public scrutiny. Accused of exploiting his marriage, he moves between courtroom, city streets and stage, carrying the weight of judgment, loyalty, and unspoken guilt. Forced to make a restrained but irreversible decision, the film observes a man whose inner truth remains elusive, caught between devotion, dignity, and loss. Harawe’s feature debut, THE VILLAGE NEXT TO PARADISE, was the first Somali film featured as an official selection of the Cannes Film Festival, where it had its world premiere in 2024. Sense of Water dir. Mohammad Rasoulof (Iran, Germany) 39 min. In the chill of exile, an Iranian writer confronts a foreign language—a language in which he must rediscover love, anger, joy, and sorrow in order to write again. His quest to reclaim the power of writing becomes an inner journey between memory and forgetting, between a lost language and a new one, where human emotion and meaning must be recreated anew. Rasoulof directed THE SEED OF THE SACRED FIG (Special Jury Prize winner at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival) and THERE IS NO EVIL (Golden Bear winner at the 2020 Berlin Film Festival), both Film Forum U.S. theatrical premieres. ---------------------------------- With one in every 70 people on earth forcibly displaced due to conflict, war, or persecution, the global community is witnessing an unprecedented crisis. The Displacement Film Fund was first conceived at the 2023 Global Refugee Forum, hosted by UNHCR and the world’s largest gathering dedicated to addressing challenges faced by refugees and their host communities. Blanchett joined forces with a group of film industry experts and creatives, all of whom have a personal connection and/or strong interest in the issue of forced displacement—and established the Fund—which launched at IFFR 2025—with a mission of giving visibility and bringing to the mainstream stories of displacement, while highlighting the diversity of displacement-related life experiences. IFFR’s Hubert Bals Fund is the Management Partner and it was founded in partnership with the Amahoro Coalition, MASTERMIND, the Tamer Family Foundation, UNIQLO and Droom en Daad. In 2026, the SP Lohia Foundation joined as Main Partner. UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency act as Strategic Partner.

screenings.description: The “cockpit” of the title is a cramped apartment in the suburbs of Tokyo, unprepossessing in size but bursting with creative ferment, for this dinky flat is functioning as the recording studio where underground producer-rapper OMSB and cohort Bim are laying down a new track, to be titled “Curve Death Match.” Shot largely from a camera locked down to the workstation and facing the duo, The Cockpit follows the songwriting process from sampling to beat-making to writing to the final recording, in the process giving an intimate, pared-to-the-bone, nuts-and-bolts breakdown of the intricacies of hip-hop artistry without rival.

Ec: Jerome Hill
screenings.description: These 35mm prints are the result of a preservation project undertaken by the Museum of Modern Art.DEATH IN THE FORENOON (1934/66, 2 min, 35mm)CANARIES (1969, 4 min, 35mm)&FILM PORTRAIT(1971, 81 min, 35mm)“FILM PORTRAIT is an autobiography in the sense that it deals explicitly with Jerome’s most personal life’s relationship to film. It draws on film clips taken in his childhood and his whole childhood involvement in art and life. It comes closest to any kind of filmic answer to Proust. […] FILM PORTRAIT is, I believe, the only direct autobiography we have in film. There is Jonas Mekas’s WALDEN, which is diary but not autobiography in a strict sense. We have Cocteau’s BLOOD OF A POET, ORPHEUS, and TESTAMENT OF ORPHEUS. One could say that this last is autobiographical, but it is also allusive and poetic; whereas Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT is a very straight attempt to present autobiography on film. Of course, subsequently, James Broughton’s TESTAMENT and my own SINCERITY & DUPLICITY series of autobiographical films were very much inspired by Jerome’s FILM PORTRAIT as well as by Jonas’s WALDEN. […] Jerome Hill’s films are great because they are poised on wit and achieve a balance – a gentle, intentional, particularly American balance.” –Stan Brakhage, FILM AT WIT’S ENDTotal running time: ca. 90 min.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: Hearing a certain tune spin on the jukebox in an all-night diner in Reno sends down-on-his-luck pianist Al Roberts (Tom Neal) on a traumatic trip down memory lane, recalling his fateful roadside encounter with Ann Savage’s aptly named femme fatale Vera and his subsequent subjugation to her, in Ulmer’s made-for-peanuts classic of noir absurdism, one of the priceless treasures to emerge from Hollywood’s so-called “Poverty Row” studios. “Possibly the bleakest, most doom-laden film noir ever… Savage’s sensational performance, combined with the real-life trajectory of Neal, who ended up going to prison for murdering his wife, have made this a tormented film with the despairing logic of nightmare.” —The Los Angeles Times

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. screenings.title: Ec: Hugo / Jacobs / Levitt / Maas
screenings.description: Ian HugoBELLS OF ATLANTIS(1952, 10 min, 16mm. Preserved by the Library of Congress through the Avant-Garde Masters program funded by The Film Foundation and administered by the National Film Preservation Foundation.)A film poem, based on Anaïs Nin’s HOUSE OF INCEST, narrated by and featuring Nin.“[BELLS OF ATLANTIS was] inspired by the prologue to my HOUSE OF INCEST and the line: ‘I remember my first birth in water.’ The film evoked the watery depths of the lost continent of Atlantis. It is a lyrical journey into prenatal memories, the theme of birth and rebirth from the sea.” –Anaïs NinKen JacobsLITTLE STABS AT HAPPINESS (1959-63, 18 min, 16mm. With Jack Smith.)“Material was cut in as it came out of the camera, embarrassing moments intact. 100’ rolls timed well with music on old 78s. I was interested in immediacy, a sense of ease, and an art where suffering was acknowledged but not trivialized with dramatics. Whimsy was our achievement, as well as breaking out of step.” –Ken JacobsHelen Levitt, Janice Loeb, and James AgeeIN THE STREET (1952, 12 min, 16mm, silent. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine
screenings.description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Paper Tiger in 35mm
screenings.description: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

screenings.title: The Shop Around the Corner (1940)
screenings.description: Alfred Kralik and Klara Novak are employees at Matuschek and Company, a general store in Budapest. Klara and Alfred are constantly at odds with each other, butting heads and disagreeing on almost everything. Both are enamored of their respective pen pals, who serve as welcome distractions in their lives. Little do they know, they are each the other's pen pal and, despite outward differences, have unwittingly fallen in love through their letters.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete

screenings.title: Night on Earth
screenings.description: Jarmusch’s career-long fascination with at-home-in-the-world wanderers finds its perfect expression in this anthology piece with a Tom Waits soundtrack and Independent Spirit Award-winning cinematography by Elmes, set simultaneously in five different cabs in five different cities around the world. In Los Angeles casting agent Gena Rowlands cross-examines driver Winona Ryder, Isaach De Bankolé drives a mysterious young blind woman through Paris, and the backseat operates everywhere as an analyst’s sofa, loneliness and urban anomie proving to know no national bounds. “Mr. Jarmusch again demonstrates his mastery of comedy of the oblique.”—The New York Times

screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
screenings.description: That the world of the future was to be increasingly shaped by Asia was a central tenet of cyberpunk, and so it should come as no surprise that one of the greatest of cyberpunk films came from the Land of the Rising Sun. Man and machine feel the urge to merge in Tsukamoto’s utterly indescribable midnight movie staple, an assault-on-the-senses body horror running of the gauntlet which centers on an anonymous salaryman who begins to transform himself into a man of steel, his waking nightmare captured in twitchy camerawork and lurid, gritty black-and-white 16mm. A symphony of sex, steel, and scarification, set to a scraping industrial clangor.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Paprika
screenings.description: The final film of visionary director Satoshi Kon (Perfect Blue, Millenium Actress), Paprika takes place in a near future where a device allows therapists to explore the dreamscapes of their patients. The head of the scientific team behind this new treatment, Atusko Chiba, creates an alter-ego named Paprika to help patients navigate their subconscious. When a thief steals the device and begins entering the minds of the public, the worlds of dreams and reality merge into a single psychedelic carnival.

screenings.description: “He has his father’s eyes…” Satanists are on the loose in Central Park West in Polanski’s slow-burn thriller, which slips almost imperceptibly from the quotidian into the profane, and gives new meaning to the phrase “pregnancy scare.” Young marrieds Mia Farrow and John Cassavetes make friendly with their elder neighbors Ruth Gordon and Sidney Blackmer, but when Farrow’s abandoned and isolated Rosemary goes into a paranoiac tailspin while expecting her first child, she begins to wonder why everyone is so very eager for her to take her daily dosage of tannis root… A masterclass in slow-building, spine-tingling suspense, aided immeasurably by the dab-handed work of legendary editor Sam O’Steen.

screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Oldboy
screenings.description: Homer with a ball-peen hammer. Kidnapped and stuffed in a hole without explanation for 15 years of solitary confinement, when Oh Dae-su (Choi Min-sik) is suddenly let loose on the streets, he’s stone-cold pissed off and very, very dangerous. Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Wild Horse Nine

screenings.description: Avant-garde designers and best friends Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil have spent 25 years working together as the NYC fashion collective threeASFOUR. screenings.title: Bitter Christmas
screenings.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant.

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two⁠-⁠time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close⁠-⁠knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice. In Norwegian, English, Romanian and Swedish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.title: Devo: Restorations and Revelations
screenings.description: COLLECTED FILM AND VIDEO WORKS 1976-84PRESENTED BY FILM RESTORATIONIST PETER CONHEIMFormed in the wreckage of the Kent State shootings in 1973, where co-founders Gerald V. Casale and Mark Mothersbaugh were students during the massacre, and still blowing the horn five decades later, Akron’s DEVO would take their subversive pop-art to staggering mainstream success. All the while, they considered themselves to be filmmakers as much as they were a “band.”From their first film onward (1976’s THE BEGINNING WAS THE END: THE TRUTH ABOUT DE-EVOLUTION), they fused their love of Dadaist image-making with their constantly shapeshifting music, confounding their record label by plowing their meager promo budgets into companion films for songs. This program unveils painstaking new restorations and reconstructions of much of this pivotal work (including SATISFACTION, FREEDOM OF CHOICE, WHIP IT, and much more) alongside a host of rarely (and never)-seen live footage, encounters with hapless interviewers, and other spud ephemera, curated specially for Anthology Film Archives by film archivist and musician Peter Conheim (Mono Pause, ex-Negativland, Wet Gate, et al).Total running time: ca. 80 min + discussion and Q&A.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Mob
screenings.description: Loosely based on the true story of Anishinaabe boy Charlie Wenjack, Cold Journey is a heart-wrenching tale of the profound pain wrought by forced assimilation, pinpointing the evils of residential schools decades before their injustices became mainstream knowledge. The only fictional feature by director Martin Defalco, the film captures its Indigenous communities in granular detail and through breathtaking images of the Canadian landscape. Featuring a stunning original song soundtrack by Indigenous musician and filmmaker Willie Dunn and a supporting turn from Chief Dan George (The Outlaw Josey Wales, Little Big Man), this is a long-overlooked but essential work of Indigenous Canadian cinema.

In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Raise the Red Lantern
screenings.description: China/Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Zhang Yimou Starring Gong Li, Saifei He, Jingwu Ma, Cuifen Cao In Mandarin with English subtitles Approx. 125 min. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul. Newly restored, RAISE THE RED LANTERN remains a landmark of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and 1990s international film. The 4K restoration of RAISE THE RED LANTERN was carried out by the Udine Far East Film Festival on the occasion of its 26th edition. The original image and sound negatives were used under the supervision of Director Zhang Yimou. The vintage positive copy, presented at the 1991 Venice International Film Festival and preserved at the Venice Biennale's Historical Archive of Contemporary Arts, was used for color reference. The restoration was made in 2024 at L'Immagine Ritrovata (Hong Kong – Bologna). Presented with support from The Reginald S. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall in 35mm
screenings.description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: He survived the Łódź Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, Theresienstadt and two death marches. Yet Marian Turski emerged from humanity's darkest chapter with a message that would challenge the world. How do educated, cultured societies descend into hatred, persecution and mass murder? And when does indifference become complicity? In XI: THOU SHALT NOT BE INDIFFERENT, Turski confronts these questions with remarkable clarity, revealing how prejudice, exclusion and the erosion of human dignity can lead to unimaginable consequences. In 1965, he joined the historic Selma-to-Montgomery civil rights march led by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., carrying the lessons of the Holocaust into a lifelong commitment to justice and equality. His extraordinary humanitarian contributions earned him prestigious international honors, including Poland's Order of Polonia Restituta and France's Légion d'honneur . His influence reached world leaders, including President Barack Obama, who personally sent greetings honoring Turski on his 90th birthday. Through intimate testimony and rare, real-life archival footage documenting the liberation of Nazi concentration camps in 1945, including historical film material by legendary filmmakers Alfred Hitchcock, Billy Wilder and Frank Capra, director and cinematographer Andrzej Wolf brings history vividly to life. The documentary pays tribute to one of the last moral compasses of the Greatest Generation. In the centennial year of Turski's birth, his warning, "Auschwitz did not fall from the sky," reminds us that history's greatest tragedies begin long before the world recognizes them. More than a story of survival, this extraordinary documentary reminds us that the past shapes the present—and that the future depends on the choices we make today. One extraordinary man. One message for all humanity. One question: Will we choose to act?

screenings.description: ASH AND CRAYONS, a documentary by Academy Award®-nominated director Evgeny Afineevsky, is an intimate portrait of childhood resilience and hope amid the war in Ukraine. The film follows seven children as they pursue their passions, support their families, build friendships, and continue moving forward with courage and determination. While rooted in the experiences of Ukrainian children, the film speaks to a universal truth: that even in the face of devastation, the human spirit has an extraordinary capacity to endure, adapt, and dream of a better tomorrow.

screenings.title: Galaxie
screenings.description: A pinnacle of the art of filmic portraiture, Gregory Markopoulos’s GALAXIE comprises thirty short portraits of men and women from across the spectrum of the mid-1960s cultural scene in New York City. Its subjects include many of Markopoulos’s fellow experimental filmmakers – Storm De Hirsch, George & Mike Kuchar, Jonas Mekas, Shirley Clarke, Amy Taubin, and Ed Emshwiller – as well as figures from the literary and art worlds, including Parker Tyler, Jasper Johns, W.H. Auden, Allen Ginsberg, Kenneth Kelman, Maurice Sendak, Susan Sontag, and others. In keeping with Markopoulos’s short-form masterpieces MING GREEN, BLISS, and SORROWS, each of the individual portraits in GALAXIE was edited entirely in-camera, a near-miraculous feat given the intricate use of multiple layers of superimposition, all of it achieved by rewinding and making additional passes through the single 100-foot (ca. 3-minute) roll of 16mm film during the shoot. Initially intending to produce only a handful of portraits, Markopoulos ended up filming 40 different chapters, and ultimately incorporated the first 30 into the completed work (presented in the order they were created). Each of the portraits represents an exquisite visual record of the encounter between subject and filmmaker, while the film as a whole provides an extraordinary opportunity to observe the gradual development of Markopoulos’s approach to portraiture and in-camera editing.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Lolita
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1962. 152 mins. 35mm. With James Mason, Shelley Winters, Peter Sellers, Sue Lyon. “How did they ever make a movie of Lolita?” the savvy, shocked poster tagline wondered. Only Stanley Kubrick would dare try. Outwitting the censors, Kubrick turned Vladimir Nabokov’s 1955 novel about a professor’s obsession with a young “nymphet” into a rich cinematic satire, emphasizing Nabokov’s dark social comedy. A monstrously proper James Mason is unforgettable as Humbert Humbert, whose twisted heart leads him to destroy his own life and soul for the love of the teenage daughter (Sue Lyon) of his crass and lovelorn landlady (Shelley Winters). As the mysterious oddball playwright Clare Quilty, Sellers lends Kubrick’s tragic satire a coherent sense of eccentricity and outlandish humor. screenings.description: German filmmaker Friedrich (Patrick Bauchau) is holed up at a hotel on the storm-lashed Portuguese coast, using American funding to shoot a shoestring budget post-apocalyptic thriller, though mostly he winds up playing a waiting game with cast and crew (including Warhol star Viva, Sam Fuller, Isabelle Weingarten, and co-writer Robert Kramer) after their producer disappears without a trace. An intermediate production made during the difficult shoot of Wenders’s 1982 Hammett for Francis Ford Coppola’s Zoetrope Studios in the US, sumptuously shot in black and white by legendary DP Henri Alekan, The State of Things is Wenders’s meditation on the complicated co-dependence of the European and American film industries.

screenings.title: Come Back to the 5 & Dime, Jimmy Dean, Jimmy Dean
screenings.description: One day in 1975, at a dusty Woolworth’s in small town McCarthy, Texas, the six members of the “Disciples of James Dean” reconvene 20 years after they first formed the club in the wake of the heartthrob actor’s death. Shifting between “present day” scenes and flashbacks to 1955 through an ingenious two-way mirror device, Altman’s film of Ed Graczyk’s play, which Altman had originally directed on the stage, is a touching meditation on dreams deferred and long-enduring female friendships, its peerless ensemble cast including Cher, Sandy Dennis, and Karen Black. Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Max Turnheim
screenings.description: Few contemporary filmmakers have demonstrated such a sustained commitment to the form of cinematic portraiture as Friedl vom Gröller, whose work is represented throughout this series. While most of her films are notably (and proudly) small in scale, MAX TURNHEIM is an exception, an ever-expanding collection of portraits of a subject she has returned to repeatedly throughout the years.“An allegorical reflection upon physiosocial existence in the world. This to-date 13-part, long-term portrait of Max Turnheim brings the abundance of Friedl vom Gröller’s gaze to complete fruition. The film conceives its portrait through the compression of an entire phase of life, including separation from the parental home, the finding of an individual path, and a renewed longing for middle class institutions. The point of departure for all this content is a face seen over the course of time.” –Alejandro BachmannCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Piano
screenings.description: Ada, mute since birth, her nine year old daughter and her piano arrive to an arranged marriage in the remote bush of nineteenth century New Zealand. Of all her belongings her husband refuses to transport the piano and it is left behind on the beach. Unable to bear its certain destruction, Ada strikes a bargain with an illiterate tattooed neighbor. She may earn her piano back if she allows him to do certain things while she plays; one black key for every lesson. The arrangement draws all three deeper and deeper into a complex emotional, sexual bond remarkable for its naïve passion and frightening disregard for limits.

screenings.title: The Muppets Take Manhattan + The Muppet Show with Liza Minnelli
screenings.description: Dir. Frank Oz. U.S., 1984, 94 mins. U.S. DCP. With Jim Henson, Dave Goelz, Jerry Nelson, Richard Hunt, Steve Whitmire, Liza Minnelli. When the Muppets’ college revue is a big hit, they decide to take the show all the way to Broadway. Adjusting to the hustle and bustle of New York City, Kermit takes a job at a local restaurant while he searches for a producer. Filled with cameos by quintessential New Yorkers, such as Gregory Hines, Joan Rivers, James Coco, Brooke Shields, and Liza Minnelli, the movie ends with a fantastical and questionably genuine wedding between Kermit and Miss Piggy. Oz’s first solo-directed film is a dose of pure joy, a true gift to showtune lovers featuring some of the greatest songs in the Muppet canon and the beloved “Muppet Babies” sequence that spawned its own mini-franchise. Rated: G Preceded by: The Muppet Show Episode 414: Starring Liza Minnelli 1979, 23 mins. Liza Minnelli brought her many talents to The Muppet Show in its fourth season in 1979. In one of the handful of episodes that broke the show’s regular variety format, Liza headlines a Muppet murder mystery as an actress who hires private eye Kermit to solve a backstage crime—her show at the Roxy has been threatened by an anonymous culprit. In between the intrigue and dead bodies that keep turning up, Liza manages to deliver some top-notch musical numbers. Can Liza and Kermit solve the crime before the villain runs out of victims? screenings.title: Minotaur
screenings.description: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in. The latest from Oscar® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times. Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence. A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, France’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 99th Academy Awards® is peerless work from an indisputable master.

screenings.title: Other People's Children
screenings.description: “Efira may be as radiant as a Botticelli angel, but it’s her no-nonsense directness that gets to you” writes TIME’s Stephanie Zacharek of the actress’s performance in the comic drama Other People’s Children as Rachel, a childless fortysomething middle-school teacher who, shortly after entering a new relationship with Ali (Roschdy Zem), the father of a four-year-old girl, finds herself increasingly besotted with the kid—and terrified of the risks that come along with such a consuming affection. A poignant, layered, and unerringly compassionate character study, featuring Efira at her most luminous and, at the same time, her most emotionally grounded.

screenings.title: Xi: Thou Shalt Not Be Indifferent
screenings.description: He survived the Łódź Ghetto, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, Theresienstadt and two death marches. In 1965, he joined the historic Selma-to-Montgomery civil rights march led by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., carrying the lessons of the Holocaust into a lifelong commitment to justice and equality. His extraordinary humanitarian contributions earned him prestigious international honors, including Poland's Order of Polonia Restituta and France's Légion d'honneur . screenings.title: Sibyl
screenings.description: Four years before her Palme d’Or triumph with Anatomy of a Fall, Triet produced this comic thriller starring Virginie Efira in the title role as a psychotherapist who, fed up with her métier, decides to return to writing fiction—and, in the person of one of her patients, a young, tumultuous actress named Margot (Adèle Exarchopoulos), finds an absolutely irresistible source of literary inspiration. Impassioned performances by both leads make Sibyl a compelling study in obsession and self-delusion, with the added inducement of Anatomy star Sandra Hüller’s appearance in a side-splitting role as the director of a film-within-the-film.

screenings.title: Gunvor Nelson Program 1
screenings.description: "“Gunvor Nelson launched her film career with a pair of raucous collage films made with her friend Dorothy Wiley. In Schmeerguntz, glamorized images of American womanhood clash with the reality of messy diapers and clogged kitchen sinks, revealing ‘a society which hides its animal functions beneath a shiny public surface’ (Film Quarterly). The surreal extravaganza Fog Pumas was a grand prize winner at the 1967 EXPRMTL festival in Knokke. My Name is Oona, perhaps Nelson’s best-known film, is an impressionistic portrait of her daughter with a memorably repetitive soundtrack partly created by Steve Reich. Kirsa Nicholina is at once a lyrical and boldly graphic birth film. Moons Pool, filmed entirely underwater with naked male and female bodies, is a dazzling example of Nelson’s visual and aural poetry. The serene Time Being is a loving, meditative film of Nelson’s mother, in bed, approaching death.” —Series curator David Schwartz

screenings.title: Ec: Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son
In the Hand of Dante + Q&A
screenings.description: In the Hand of Dante follows the parallel lives of a New York author (Nick Tosches) in the 21st century who embarks on a violent journey after he is recruited by a mafia don to steal Italian poet Dante Alighieri’s The Divine Comedy written in the poet’s own hand, and Dante in the 14th century seeking inspiration to write his most important work – each man unknowingly connected through time and their obsessive quest for love, beauty, and the divine.

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Screenwriter Lawrence Kasdan paid tribute to Double Indemnity with his directorial debut. When the summertime Florida heat enables lawyer William Hurt to scratch an itch with housewife Kathleen Turner, what is there to do about her husband Richard Crenna? Murder, of course! Confidently combining classical storytelling and contemporary sizzle, Body Heat satisfied audiences with a taste for steamy noir stylings and catapulted its two leads into the Hollywood A-list. For Turner in particular (making her feature film debut), Body Heat was the beginning of her reign as one of the queens of 80s cinema.

screenings.title: Paths of Glory
screenings.description: Preceded by Kubrick’s documentary short The Seafarers (1953, 30 mins) Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1957. 88 mins. 35mm. With Kirk Douglas, Ralph Meeker, Adolphe Menjou, George Macready, Wayne Morris, Richard Anderson. One of the bleakest anti-war films ever made, Stanley Kubrick’s brilliant World War I drama about the abuse of military hierarchy drives home its message in every aspect of its construction, from its mechanized tracking shots through trenches to its disturbingly protracted climax. Paths of Glory represents the first full expression of Kubrick’s style, but it also is the last of his films to center around a wholly virtuous hero (Douglas) and the last to view the human individual as a bulwark of decency in an inhuman world. screenings.title: ACE Presents: Ghost World
screenings.description: The first film adaptation from the work of caustic cartoonist Daniel Clowes, Ghost World is a post-apocalyptic survival film set in the suburban AnyAmerica of 2001. Thora Birch and Scarlett Johansson co-star as two too-smart girls, freshly matriculated from high school and rudderless in early adulthood, who employ scalding irony as a ward to fend off the toxic effects of existence in a cultural wasteland, discovering an amiably creepy kindred spirit in the form of Steve Buscemi’s weedy record collector, Seymour. An anthem for opting out and modern-day classic, with editor Michael R. Miller displaying the gift for mordant, off-kilter comedy he’d honed working with the Coen Brothers.

screenings.title: Secrets & Lies
screenings.description: The winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1996 Cannes Film Festival, Leigh’s tender, funny, fearless film has Brenda Blethyn in a career-best performance as Cynthia, a white working-class woman who has a life-changing revelation when she meets Black middle-class optometrist Marianne Jean-Baptiste, who informs Cynthia she’s the little girl Cynthia had given up for adoption 27 years ago, all grown up. Developed, like all of Leigh’s films, through a process of collaborative improvisation, it’s a film of startling spontaneity and uncomfortable, unflinching emotional honesty.

screenings.title: Film No. 5 (smile)
screenings.description: “[S]hot with a high-speed camera…FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) reveals John Lennon’s face, recorded at 333 frames per second for an extended duration, outdoors, in color, and accompanied by a sound track of outdoor sounds recorded at the same time the imagery was recorded. FILM NO. 5 (SMILE) divides roughly into two halves, one continuous shot each. During the first half, the film is a meditation on Lennon’s face, which is so still that on first viewing I wasn’t entirely sure for a while that the film was live action and not an optically printed photograph of Lennon smiling slightly. Though almost nothing happens in any conventional sense, however, the intersection of the high speed filming and our extended gaze creates continuous, subtle transformations. […] While the second shot is more active than the first, the amount of activity remains minimal by conventional standards (and unusually so even for avant-garde film). It is as though those of us in the theater and Lennon are meditating on each other from opposite sides of the cinematic apparatus, joined together by Ono in a lovely, hypnotic stasis.” –Scott MacDonald, “Yoko Ono: Ideas on Film”Preceded by:Yoko OnoFLUXFILM NO. 16: aka NO. 4: BOTTOMS1966, 6 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent. Camera: Jeff Perkins, Anthony Cox. Starring: Susannah Campbell, Philip Corner, Anthony Cox, Bici Hendricks, Geoffrey Hendricks, Kyoko Ono, Yoko Ono, Ben Patterson, Jeff Perkins, Susan Poland, Jerry Sablo, Carolee Schneemann, James Tenney, Pieter Vanderbeck, Verne Williams.“The rebellious, erotic, liberatory nature of the film, which reflects the tenor of Fluxus, acts in direct opposition to the nineteenth-century scientific treatment of the body as a ‘dynamic field of action in need of regulation and control.’” –Chrissie Iles, “Erotic Conceptualism: The Films of Yoko Ono”Total running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: 35mm Import. Praised by François Truffaut, Kumashiro’s acclaimed period drama concerns the affairs of men and women within the fusuma-walled interiors of a Taisho pleasure house, all the while courting Kumashiro’s stance on censorship and the genre’s legal trials.

screenings.title: The Year of Living Dangerously
screenings.description: Dir. Peter Weir. 1983, 115 mins. Australia/U.S./Philippines. 35mm. With Mel Gibson, Sigourney Weaver, Linda Hunt. Bembol Rocco, Michael Murphy. Operating at the height of his storytelling powers, and following his international successes with Picnic at Hanging Rock and Gallipoli, Australian director Peter Weir took a big swing with this sweeping yet intimate historical drama. Set in Indonesia in the mid-sixties in the lead-up to the overthrow of President Sukarno’s government, Weir’s adaptation of Christopher Koch’s acclaimed novel centers around an Australian journalist (Gibson) and his romantic relationship with a British embassy officer (Weaver) and his professional one with a Chinese Australian photojournalist (Hunt, in an Oscar-winning performance). Suspenseful, romantic, and intelligent, the film predicted Weir’s remarkable run in Hollywood, yet stands on its own as a singular 1980s entertainment that traffics in politically complex themes with nuance and depth. screenings.title: Demons
screenings.description: Dir. Lamberto Bava. 1985, 88 min. DCP. With Natasha Hovey, Michele Soavi, Paolo Cazzo, Urbano Barberini, Karl Zinny. While attending the premiere of a horror movie, friends Cheryl (Hovey) and Kathy (Cazzo) find themselves trapped in the cinema from hell. Reality begins to imitate the film on the screen as members of the audience transform into ravenous demons and go on the rampage. A collaboration by producer Dario Argento and director Lamberto Bava, Demons is a marvel of bloody special effects by two Italian horror maestros that satirizes the idea that the Devil is lurking in every corner of the pop culture young people consume, waiting to corrupt and possess them. screenings.title: Barbara
screenings.description: With Jeanne Balibar, Mathieu Amalric, Vincent Peirani, Aurore Clement, and Grégoire Colin.Amalric’s seventh feature-length film as a director is both a heartfelt tribute to the legendary chanteuse Barbara (1930-97), and a vehicle for another peerlessly talented French luminary, the actress and singer Jeanne Balibar. Amalric’s films are remarkable for their intuitive freedom, and their emphasis on emotional textures and states of feeling rather than on straightforward narrative construction or easily grasped meanings. BARBARA is a case in point: eschewing anything like a coherent, birth-to-death account of the events of her life, the film instead orchestrates fragments of the singer’s life and performances into a free and quasi-abstract meditation on Barbara’s identity and cultural presence. And by casting Balibar not as Barbara per se but more self-referentially as an actress making a film-within-the-film about the singer, his film becomes an even broader investigation into the concept of biographical filmmaking, representation, and identity. An experimental biopic in the tradition of Stanley Kwan’s CENTER STAGE, Peter Watkins’s EDVARD MUNCH, and Paul Leduc’s FRIDA, it features a typically riveting, charismatic performance from Balibar.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

Theatrical premiere of a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: The Ascent
screenings.description: The bloodthirsty and seemingly unstoppable Nazi war machine is on the march towards Moscow in Shepitko’s wrenching, snow-swept World War II drama, which begins with two Soviet peasant soldiers foraging for food in a Belarusian village and proceeds to tell an emotional, lyrical tale of loyalty and betrayal, partisanship and collaboration, and, ultimately, the possibility of transcendent redemption. Shepitko’s final feature, frequently cited as among the greatest of Soviet films, won the Golden Bear at the 1977 Berlin Film Festival, just two years before its director’s tragic death in a car accident at age 41.
